reviewed_hash_basis: sha256 over epic-gate.sh + plan-batches.test.sh + docs/HOOKS.md concatenated in that order; reproduced by the reviewer (hash_reproduced=yes) and independently by the orchestrator
stop_condition: each round-4 fix re-verified as new code; the rewritten degradation path reviewed as new code because it is the safety net; every extraction on the plan path audited for rc-AND-shape discipline; four-part pairing applied to every META leg

r4_fix_assessment.basis: PLAN-BATCHES-ALIAS-CARDINALITY-GATE at :1489-1500 computes the declared pair count with guarded jq, rejects nonnumeric/empty, and compares all three alias-array lengths against it.
The validate-design ladder at :1220 now tests both vout_rc and vshape_ok.
Control-char computation checks rc and array shape; the sentinel rejects 0x00-0x1f/0x7f with declared_path_contains_control_chars at :1295-1323.
Both remaining jq assignments in _pb_degrade use cmd || rc=$?; a nonzero schedule or extraction reaches _pb_finish with batches=[] and an observation annotation.

The explicit lexical fallback is deleted and topo-computation failure emits no schedule. BUT degradation occurring before bindings are published still treats an empty task-to-unit map as 'no edges' and emits lexical order, which can still invert a real dependency. See R5-F4.
EG is globally $CANON/epic-gate.sh at plan-batches.test.sh:277 and assertion 0.1 pins that identity. Orchestrator-verified independently.
Section 4A replaces the actual intersection predicate with select(true) and asserts conflicting units co-batch; 4B is separately and accurately scoped to failure handling.
Section 9n builds three real children, publishes two valid bindings with a known dependency, leaves the third unbound to reach _pb_degrade, and independently targets both remaining jq sites.

findings.description: Status and validator shape gates check only field PRESENCE, then compare jq -r output textually to 'true'. So satisfied:"true" or ok:"true" (JSON strings) are accepted exactly like JSON booleans, letting a malformed validator supply usable unit data and obtain parallel_safe=true.
findings.evidence: Reviewer ran inline literal probes: both has(...) predicates return rc 0 for string-valued booleans, and jq -r renders those strings as 'true', satisfying the downstream shell comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Require exact types in the gates: .satisfied|type=="boolean", .ok|type=="boolean", string for hashes/paths/error keys, array for unit_ids, object for unit_files/unit_deps.

findings.description: Several plan-path jq encoders and aggregations remain unguarded under set -e. A targeted jq failure while building a problem/binding entry, bound_pairs_json or problems_json exits the script before _pb_degrade/_pb_finish, producing NO named serial degradation envelope at all.
findings.evidence: Unguarded jq substitutions inside problem_entries+=("$(jq ...)"), bound_entries+=("$(jq ...)"), bound_pairs_json=$(...), problems_json=$(...). Probe: bash -c 'set -e; a+=("$(false)")' exits 1 without reaching the next command.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard every encoder/aggregation with an explicit rc variable routing failure to _pb_degrade set_computation_failed; do not hide jq inside array-assignment or printf arguments.

findings.description: Two not-yet-existing paths that are Unicode-normalisation-equivalent or non-ASCII-case-equivalent can co-batch even where they name the same eventual file. The code documents this residual; the release invariant and docs claim unconditional file-set non-intersection.
findings.evidence: Neither alias pass can detect these spellings when neither path exists. The only case check is ascii_downcase; the inode check is gated by -e. The batching predicate then compares original strings byte-for-byte and treats them as disjoint.
findings.suggested_fix: DECIDED BY OPERATOR: narrow the CLAIM to match the code rather than over-degrade. State exactly what holds (byte-identical, symlink, inode, ASCII case-equivalent are caught; normalisation-equivalent/non-ASCII-case-equivalent where NEITHER path exists are not). Rejected alternative: fail closed on all non-ASCII declared paths, which over-degrades every project with a non-ASCII filename and cannot be narrowed later under bash 3.2 without new machinery.

findings.description: An early degradation occurring AFTER dependencies are extracted but BEFORE child bindings are published can emit a dependent before its prerequisite. With _PB_DEGRADE_DEPS_JSON populated and _PB_DEGRADE_BINDINGS_JSON still [], _pb_degrade maps every child to null, derives every dependency list as empty, and emits LC_ALL=C-sorted child order. This is why R4-F5 is only partially fixed.
findings.evidence: Control-char, canonical-path, case-collision and alias degradations all fire after dependency publication at :1254 but before binding publication at :1596. In the topological jq, an absent task-to-unit mapping takes the `if $u == null then []` arm, so T-A-DEPENDENT precedes T-Z-PREREQ despite the artifact carrying the dependency and the binding records being available but unread.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve and publish clean bindings before any post-validation guard can emit a degraded schedule, OR refuse with batches=[] whenever artifact dependencies exist but a complete task-to-unit mapping is unavailable.

findings.description: _pb_finish treats any nonempty successful result from emit_plan_batches as valid. A malfunctioning jq exiting 0 with whitespace, [], null or malformed text bypasses the jq-independent fallback and is persisted and printed as the envelope.
findings.evidence: The only post-call test is [ -z "$out" ]; there is no JSON or envelope-shape validation. Section 9h injects only an exit-1 jq, so it cannot discriminate this successful-wrong-output shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Check emit rc AND validate the complete required envelope shape before persistence; route nonobject, unparsable or wrong-field/type output to the jq-independent fallback.

findings.description: The rewritten degradation extraction accepts sched_batches=[] as a successfully computed schedule even when child count is positive; its only content check is nonempty shell text, so a successful-but-empty extraction gets no refusal annotation.
findings.evidence: Inline probe of the exact extraction filter against {"ok":true,"batches":[]} returned [] with rc 0; at :1009 [ -n "$sched_batches" ] is true so batches is assigned without checking cardinality against $#. Section 9n injects only nonzero failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate that the extracted array has exactly $# singleton batches containing each expected task exactly once and no extras; otherwise retain batches=[] and append the schedule-computation refusal annotation.

non_discriminating.why: Its named SPECIFIC MISBEHAVIOUR is now batches=[], which is the SAFE refusal required when ordering is unavailable. It no longer demonstrates a dependency-order violation; the separate shipped control is the only ordering assertion.
The injected jq only exits nonzero, so the leg still passes while _pb_finish lacks successful-wrong-shape validation; its broad 'malfunction' label does not cover rc-0 malformed output.
The shim exercises only an rc-1 extraction; it does not discriminate the successful [] result accepted by [ -n "$sched_batches" ].

notes: No specs executed (an L2 suite was running concurrently). Reviewer used shasum, bash -n, rg, nl/sed, literal-inline jq probes and short in-memory errexit probes. Sections 4 and 7 DO print a line-initial '  SKIP:' and increment SKIPPED_SECTIONS when python3 is absent, and the final summary exposes the count - the vacuity concern raised in round 4 is genuinely closed. The Unicode alias finding follows the implementation's own documented residual; no filesystem-writing reproduction was attempted in the read-only sandbox.
